The reused smContextRef names another UE's context, which the request then deletes.
note: R1 is right: 29.501 4.4.1 has no modal verb on reuse ('A URI uniquely identifies a resource.'); 23.527 6.2.1 calls the NRF procedures 'optional procedures that may be supported' and 6.2.3 says the profile 'may include the recoveryTime attribute'.

old: TS~24.501 \S6.4.1.7~\cite{ts24501}: for an initial request with a PSI already in use, the SMF ``shall locally release the existing PDU session''. Local release means no 5GSM signalling to the UE; it does not waive the N4 Session Release that releasing a session includes (TS~23.502 \S4.3.4.2, step~2a~\cite{ts23502}), and the pinned SMF sends none.
new: TS~29.502 \S5.2.2.2.1~\cite{ts29502}: before it creates a context that collides with one of the same SUPI and PSI, the SMF ``should delete the existing SM context locally and any associated resources in the UPF, PCF, CHF, and UDM''; the pinned SMF sends no PFCP deletion, so it departs from this ``should''. TS~24.501 \S6.4.1.7~\cite{ts24501} adds that the SMF ``shall locally release the existing PDU session''. A local release omits signalling to the UE and ``can include communication among network entities''; the release procedure of TS~23.502 \S4.3.4.2~\cite{ts23502} includes the N4 Session Release (step~2a), but that text describes another procedure.
note: The clause R1 suggested is verified against ETSI TS 129 502 V18.12.0 and its verb is 'should'. The 24.501 quote is verbatim (6.4.1.7 c)); the definition 'Local release' and its NOTE 6 are in 24.501 clause 3.1. So the behaviour departs from a 'should'; reading the 24.501 'shall' as requiring N4 deletion is an interpretation.

If the SMF clears the session without the Reject, as the log signature indicates, it departs from TS~24.501 \S6.4.1.4.1~\cite{ts24501} (``The SMF shall send the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT message''), and the AMF keeps a PSI whose SM context is gone. old: It distinguishes explicit protocol obligations from the reject-teardown race, for which no clause names the behaviour and the claim rests on $\Robs$ alone.
new: Only the stalled release departs from a ``shall'' whose precondition our records establish. The orphan sessions depart from a ``should''. The reject-teardown race departs from a ``shall'' only if its unreproduced signature holds. Cross-UE deletion and the registration reject depart from no mandatory text and rest on our criteria (Table~\ref{tab:standards}).

TS~24.501 \S5.4.5.2.5 has the AMF release a PDU session locally when the UE sends an initial request for a PSI that the AMF still holds, which covers the dangling references if the T3580 retransmissions are such requests.
